newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar ends higher, March holds $300.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar ends higher, March holds $300.

text.p: White sugar futures remained higher during Wednesday evening trading, finishing in the plus column with spot March supported above $300.

Traders reported a mostly routine session, with activity mixed on both sides of the market. Prices generally consolidated after follow-through selling expected after initial weakness on the spot position did not emerge.
With firmer raws, the spot premium remained broadly in line with Tuesday's close as New York consolidated after its recent sharp falls and funds held onto their long positions.
March ended up $1.90 at $301.00 after opening at $299.00, while May closed up $1.90 also at $300.60. Turnover was 2,110 lots.
Nearby spreads narrowed as both May and August edged up above $300. March/May was reported to have traded at flat during the afternoon.
European sugar traders said they expected the results of Libya's buying tender by 1200 GMT on Thursday although the decision had been initially scheduled for Wednesday.

Turkey's state refiner Turkseker said it was still assessing bids for its tender to export 50,000 tonnes of whites, which could be concluded early on Thursday. A Turkseker official said it might consider splitting the offer into two or three parts.

Bidders are said to include local food and commodities traders Lebsan, Baykur, Naptat, Yilmazlar, Rotel, Ram and Fissan. E D & F Man and Andre have been named among the few international companies which participated.
Local traders said prices from some competing local companies ran as high as a $20 premium over Paris futures.
The Paris exchange has announced two adjustments to the delivery process of its white sugar futures contract, to apply to the March and May 1998 expiries and onwards.
The seller of a contract may now deliver sugar either in polyjute or polypropylene bags. If polypropylene bags are chosen then the buyer is paid a packing differential.
The seller will be obliged specify either polyjute or polypropylene bags for delivery and to deliver a minimum net quantity of 2,500 tonnes.
